metadata.source: Vendor publications, peer-reviewed papers, spec sheets
metadata.description: DiVincenzo Criteria assessment for major quantum computing platforms. The 5 core criteria (plus 2 networking) define hardware viability for fault-tolerant quantum computing.

core.name: Scalable Physical Qubits
core.description: A well-characterized qubit system that can scale to many qubits

core.name: Initialization
core.description: Ability to initialize qubits to a known state

core.name: Long Coherence Times
core.description: Decoherence time much longer than gate operation time

core.name: Universal Gate Set
core.description: A complete set of quantum gates for arbitrary operations

core.name: Qubit-Specific Measurement
core.description: Ability to measure individual qubits reliably

networking.name: Stationary-Flying Interconversion
networking.description: Interconversion between stationary and flying qubits

networking.name: Flying Qubit Transmission
networking.description: Faithful transmission of flying qubits between locations

not_demonstrated.label: Not Demonstrated
not_demonstrated.description: No public demonstration of this capability

partial.label: Partial
partial.description: Early demonstrations but not yet at scale or production quality

demonstrated.label: Demonstrated
demonstrated.description: Capability proven in production or peer-reviewed experiments

scalable.label: Scalable
scalable.description: Demonstrated at scale with clear path to fault-tolerant operation

C1.evidence: Heron R2: 156 qubits in heavy-hexagonal lattice; Condor: 1,121 qubits demonstrated

C2.evidence: Active reset achieves <0.1% residual excited-state population within 34 ns

C3.evidence: T1 ~100 us median, best qubits ~300 us; T2/gate ratio ~250-500x

C4.evidence: Native CZ, RZ, SX, X gates on Heron; 5,000 two-qubit gate circuits demonstrated

C5.evidence: Dispersive readout per qubit; simultaneous multi-qubit measurement with mid-circuit capability

N1.evidence: Microwave-to-optical transduction via GaP cavity demonstrated in lab (IBM Zurich)

N2.evidence: Cryogenic chip-to-chip coupling at short range only; optical fiber transmission not demonstrated

C1.evidence: Willow: 105 qubits with below-threshold error correction proving scaling viability

C2.evidence: Co-optimized reset integrated into error correction cycles at 1.1 us cycle time

C3.evidence: T1 ~100 us (5x over Sycamore); logical memory lifetime exceeds physical by 2.4x

C4.evidence: Native sqrt(iSWAP), CZ gates; 1Q fidelity 99.97%, 2Q fidelity 99.88% average

C5.evidence: Readout fidelity ~99.3% simultaneous; real-time decoding at 63 us latency (distance-5)

N1.evidence: No public microwave-to-optical transduction work; focus on single-chip QEC

N2.evidence: Same fundamental transduction challenge as all superconducting platforms

C1.evidence: Helios (Nov 2025): 98 physical qubits delivering 94 error-detected and 48 error-corrected logical qubits; clear path to Apollo / fully fault-tolerant by 2030

C2.evidence: Optical pumping initialization with qubit reuse and mid-circuit re-initialization

C3.evidence: Yb+ coherence times of seconds (stationary); T2/gate ratio >10,000x

C4.evidence: All-to-all connectivity; Helios delivers beyond break-even QEC with 2Q 99.9%+; logical error rates 10-100x below physical; mid-circuit measurement + conditional logic; iceberg codes implemented

C5.evidence: SPAM fidelity >99.75%; individual fluorescence detection with mid-circuit branching commercially available

N1.evidence: Lab demonstrations of ion-photon entanglement; Apollo architecture planned with photonic links

N2.evidence: Academic ion-photon entanglement distribution across traps (NIST/Oxford heritage)

C1.evidence: Forte: 36 qubits (single chain); Tempo: 100 qubits expected; scaling requires photonic interconnects

C2.evidence: Optical pumping to ground hyperfine state; Ba+ platform achieves 99.96% state prep

C3.evidence: T1: 10-100 s; T2 up to 4,200 s with dynamical decoupling; T2/gate ratio ~100,000x

C4.evidence: XX/ZZ native gates; 1Q fidelity 99.98%; 2Q fidelity 99.6% (Yb+), 99.9% (Ba+ dev)

C5.evidence: Individual ion fluorescence detection; SPAM fidelity 99.5% (Forte), 99.96% (Ba+ dev)

N1.evidence: Ion-photon entanglement (Feb 2024); remote ion-ion entanglement via photonic link (Oct 2024)

N2.evidence: Photon transmission between trap nodes with entanglement swapping; milestone 2 of 4 achieved

C1.evidence: Omega chipset has all components for million-qubit systems in semiconductor fab; no multi-qubit processor yet

C2.evidence: Dual-rail photonic qubit state preparation fidelity 99.98% with deterministic photon source

C3.evidence: Photons don't decohere traditionally; loss is dominant error (~1% per stage, down from ~50%)

C4.evidence: Interferometer fidelity 99.999%; 2Q fusion fidelity 99.22%; full fault-tolerant circuit not demonstrated

C5.evidence: On-chip SNSPDs with 99.98% SPAM fidelity; measurement is inherent in photonic detection

N1.evidence: Photonic qubits are natively flying qubits; no modality conversion needed

N2.evidence: Chip-to-chip qubit transmission over optical fiber at 99.72% fidelity up to 250 m
